B1.recipe: just bootstrap <inputs.json>, on the prepared interpreter
B1.what: the bootstrap is WRITTEN. tools/bootstrap.py validates the operator's selections and names every missing one at once BEFORE anything durable, composes the Authority (principals derived, Works created, three route handlers, four grants per Work in its own scope), lays out the external state, emits the stage-execution document as /1 or /2 with job_bindings, reports configured capacity, and prints the four exports. It selects nothing, submits no Job and executes nothing. Repeating it preserves state and refuses a conflicting binding before the Authority is even opened.

E1.note: the checks RUN `just`; reading the recipe is what let the wrong spelling survive
E1.what: the interpreter override is POSITIONAL. `just setup /path/to/python3`, in the recipe comment, the runbook and both refusals. Reproduced first with real just expansion: `just --dry-run setup PY=/usr/bin/python3.13` expands to --python "PY=/usr/bin/python3.13", and `just --dry-run version PY=...` against the sibling justfile is refused as an unknown recipe, so the variable spelling is not an override here either.

E2.what: ownership is published BEFORE the install and records `installed`. A tool-created environment whose install has not succeeded is `incomplete`: setup RESUMES it without recreating, `interpreter` refuses it, and a genuinely foreign or incompatible directory is still refused and still never deleted. Ready is published only after the locked install succeeds.
